title: Solids, liquids and gases
keyIdea: We group materials as solids, liquids or gases by how they behave: keep shape, flow, or spread out.

kid: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow and can be poured. Gases spread out to fill a space.
Sand can pour, but each grain is a tiny solid. It keeps its shape.
adult: Grouping by behaviour: does it keep its own shape (solid), flow and keep the same volume (liquid), or spread out to fill any container (gas)? Gases can be squashed; liquids and solids hardly can.
Powders such as sand and flour pour like liquids but are solids, because each grain keeps its shape. Gases are often invisible, so we notice them by smell or by what they push (wind, bubbles).

familyTip: Squeeze a syringe of air, then a syringe of water (outside, with care). Which one squashes?

practice.prompt: Sand pours. Is it a liquid?
choices: No, each grain is a solid
practice.explain: Each grain keeps its shape: sand is a solid.
Gas particles are far apart, so gases squash.
